mission_1.search: The lengths are equal: both are 13.5 m. A* examined fewer cells (700 vs 928 for BFS). My BFS uses a queue, so it checks cells in every direction evenly. My A* uses a heap with g + heuristic, so it checks the cells closest to the goal first. The heuristic only guides the search, so the route is still the shortest.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, DFS's path was much longer than BFS's (104 m vs 24.5 m). My DFS uses a stack and takes the first route it finds, not the shortest one. IDDFS ended as resource_limit because it restarts at every depth and repeats work until the budget runs out. On the unreachable map, all four (BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*) returned no_path. no_path means the search finished and found no route. resource_limit means the search was stopped early, so we don't know if a route exists. I used AI to run through my code to check if there was bugs I could not point out. There was a few logic gaps that it explained to me and I fixed my code.  Then I ran small tests and the full table. BFS and A* matched at the shortest length, and DFS was longer.
